Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
Redwood + Midsail weekly POC sync focused on mid-sprint go/no-go gating, explicit cutover steps and A/B/Canary traffic plan. Security asked for KMS/audit details and confirmation that no KV-cache persists PII. Action owners identified and due dates set.

Topics:

- Cutover checklist: preflight, warm-up, traffic gates, rollback criteria

--- Transcript ---
00:00 Samir Patel: ok hey everyone thanks for joining, I see most of us, we'll run about 45 to 60 minutes, got a tight agenda but try to be pragmatic. Jenna I'll hand over to you for the quick results recap, is that cool?
00:15 Jenna Liu: yeah quick recap; we ran the synthetic generator against the staging cluster last night, 10k tokens per sec burst, overall p50 is 210 ms, p95 sits at 1.4s on the large model, smaller quantized variant p95 around 850ms, error-rate was— was essentially zero, a couple of timeouts when we hit cold KV cash — cache — KV cache warmup, so that's just the warm up issue.
00:46 Carlos Mendes: sorry can I ask, when you say "large model" which checkpoint are we talking— is that the 7B dense you onboarded or the 13B quant?
00:55 Jenna Liu: good call, that was the 13B fp16 baseline on our dedicated pool, and the 7B quant is the lower-latency variant. We also tested trunked longer sequences and saw compounding p95s beyond 2.2s for sequences over 1k tokens, so we recommend sequence-length gating on the canary.
01:20 Priya Kapoor: sequence gating, hmm. For our product most requests are 150–300 tokens but there will be spikes. How would we enforce gating? Rate limit or reject?
01:33 Jenna Liu: options: 1) prefix-based reject for >512 tokens during canary; 2) route long sequences to a slower pool as fallback; 3) allow but mark as "background" with lower SLA. We'll map to your success criteria.
01:48 Samir Patel: also note that intelligent prefix/KV caching helps — you saw the warm-up; if you do a warm-up run in preflight we can almost eliminate those cold spots.
01:58 James O'Neal: warm-up run— what's the recommended pattern? Simulate 15 minutes at 20% traffic?
02:06 Jenna Liu: yep exactly, a staged ramp: 5 minutes at 5%, 10 at 20, 10 at 50 then the canary window. Use same seed workload. We'll provide a script.
02:18 Marco Alvarez: I'll post the warm-up script + example commands after the call.
02:22 Ellen Ross: quick security question — you mentioned KV cache, does any of that persist PII or do we need to scrub? Also around KMS, are you using our KMS or Redwood-managed?
02:35 Samir Patel: good question— in the POC the cache is ephemeral inside the runtime; we don't persist KV to disk. For Private setups you can plug your own KMS; for Dedicated we can integrate customer-managed KMS via KMIP or your cloud KMS. For this POC we used Redwood-managed keys but we can switch.
02:55 Ellen Ross: can you put that in writing, maybe a one pager for audit— key rotation, who can access audit logs, retention windows?
03:03 Samir Patel: sure, I'll include a security appendix.
03:07 Carlos Mendes: back to canary traffic — I'm trying to understand risk. If we do a 5% canary for three hours and metrics look fine, are we confident to go to 50% in an hour after? What's the playbook?
03:20 Jenna Liu: recommended playbook: 5% for 30–60 minutes with triggered checks every 5 minutes (latency p50/p95, error-rate delta, model output regression signal), then 20% for 30 minutes, then 50% for 20 minutes. If any gate trips, automatic rollback to the previous variant. We propose conservative thresholds: p95 increase >25% or error-rate >0.5% or regression score drop >3 points triggers stop & rollback.
03:54 Priya Kapoor: regression score— remind me how that's computed?
03:59 Jenna Liu: we compare a fixed prompt set (the eval-suite we curated) and measure top-level metrics — pass/fail for hallucination checks, answer similarity, and a quality score. It's not perfect but it's a fast signal.
04:12 Carlos Mendes: can we include a few of our own prompts in that suite?
04:15 Jenna Liu: absolutely, you should. Add them to the shared eval doc.
04:18 Marco Alvarez: link will go out in chat.
04:21 James O'Neal: who is responsible for abort if the canary trips—we need an escalation path, page someone?
04:28 Samir Patel: operationally Redwood can do automated rollback if thresholds trip; but we'll also designate on-call owners: Midsail SRE (James) owns the customer rollback trigger, Redwood SE (Jenna) owns observability tuning, and Samir will own stakeholder comms. We'll put names in runbook.
04:46 Ellen Ross: and legal/compliance wants an auditable action log for any switching — is that native?
04:52 Jenna Liu: yes we ship an audit trail for rollouts (who initiated, timestamps, traffic splits). We can push logs to your SIEM via the webhook.
04:59 Priya Kapoor: about A/B — is there a case for doing an A/B instead of staged canary? We want to test two different prompt-engineering strategies in prod.
05:09 Jenna Liu: you can do A/B but keep in mind A/B splits double the complexity for interpreting drift; A/B is great for UX/response content experiments, canary is safer for model variant swap. You could run an A/B under the canary umbrella (A/B at 5% to compare two prompts) then promote the winner.
05:27 Carlos Mendes: ok that might work, run A/B within canary. How about telemetry — what dashboards should we watch?
05:34 Jenna Liu: per-route dashboards: token throughput, p50/p95, model-token count, error-rate, cold-start ratio, and a regression score. We'll add an 'entropy' or hallucination counter if you enable the eval hooks.
05:48 James O'Neal: alerting windows— are you suggesting 5 minute or 1 minute windows? For canaries I prefer short windows to catch spikes fast but also smoothing to avoid noisy rollbacks.
05:59 Jenna Liu: suggest dual windows: 1-minute for burst detection with a suppression rule requiring sustained 3 consecutive windows to trigger automated rollback; 5-minute for aggregated thresholds used for manual review.
06:13 Samir Patel: also plan a quiet window for noise — do a quiet time on downstream jobs before cutover to reduce false positives.
06:20 Priya Kapoor: runbook specifics— we need a checklist that covers preflight (configs, DNS, keys), warm-up, canary windows, monitoring, and rollback steps. And a single command to flip traffic if needed.
06:33 Jenna Liu: we'll give you a runbook with one-click steps for traffic shift (we use a small orchestration shim that calls the routing API), plus a manual rollback curl sample.
06:41 Marco Alvarez: I'll attach the sample curl and the runbook links.
06:45 Carlos Mendes: about data retention— how long are logs kept for this pilot and where?
06:49 Samir Patel: default 30 days in hosted logs; we can extend retention for Dedicated or export logs to your S3 for long-term. For Private you control retention.
06:59 Ellen Ross: please include PII scoping— which fields are redacted client-side.
07:03 Samir Patel: noted. We'll add a table with PII fields and redaction behavior.
07:08 James O'Neal: rehearsal plan— can we do a blue/green rehearsal in staging next Wednesday? We'd like to run the full traffic shift and rollback with the load-test harness.
07:18 Samir Patel: Wednesday is fine, Jenna free to run with James?
07:21 Jenna Liu: yep let's schedule it, I'll own the script execution and analysis.
07:25 Priya Kapoor: final ask: can you include an explicit SLA degradation table — e.g., expected extra cost if hitting p95 at x ms — we need to present this to finance.
07:36 Samir Patel: we can provide cost delta estimates for different batch/quantization knobs. I'll include rough numbers in the runbook appendix.
07:45 Carlos Mendes: great. Anything else?
07:48 Marco Alvarez: two quick items — I'll create a dedicated shared folder for cutover artifacts and a 'go-decision' checklist that requires signoff from SRE + Security + Product.
07:58 Samir Patel: perfect. To wrap, recap of owners — Samir: runbook & security appendix; Jenna: canary thresholds and warm-up script; Marco: shared folder & runbook link; James/Ellen: validate infra and security doc. We'll reconvene after the staging rehearsal with results.
08:17 Carlos Mendes: ok thanks everyone, appreciate the clarity.
08:19 Samir Patel: thanks, we'll follow up with the artifacts. Bye.
